stem.en: Nitrogen has 5 valence electrons. How many shared pairs join the two atoms in an N₂ molecule?

text.en: 1 pair, because one shared pair is enough to make a bond.
2 pairs, because every gas molecule has a double bond, as oxygen does.
3 pairs, because each atom needs 3 more electrons to reach 8.
5 pairs, because each atom shares all its valence electrons.

explanation.en: Each nitrogen atom has 5 valence electrons and needs 3 more for an octet, so each shares 3. That makes 3 shared pairs, a triple bond, drawn N≡N. Each atom then counts 8: its 2 unshared electrons plus the 6 in the bond. With 1 pair, each atom would have only 6. Oxygen has a double bond because it needs 2, and hydrogen and chlorine gases have single bonds, so not every gas is the same. Sharing all 5 would give each atom 10, more than an octet.

hints.en: Count how many electrons one nitrogen atom needs to reach 8. Each shared pair adds one to its count.
